skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

4. // Memory Region — Specifications
5. //
6. // A memory region is a contiguous, non-wrapping half-open byte interval of the
7. // address space, `[start, start + size)`, tagged with metadata
8. // (type / permissions / cache policy). `TruncatedMemoryRegion<T>` is the same
9. // interval additionally constrained so both endpoints are page-aligned, making
10. // it directly usable for frame/page booking. Both region types share the single
11. // `MemoryRegionView` abstraction (the truncated wrapper forwards `view()` to its
12. // inner region).
13. //
14. // Addresses are abstracted to `int` through the universal `spec_addr` projection
15. // (defined in `page.spec.rs`, `pub uninterp spec fn spec_addr<T: Address>`),
16. // exactly as `PageAligned<T>` does. Using `spec_addr` — rather than a
17. // `T: View<V = int>` bound on the `View` impl — is what lets the `View` (and the
18. // `@`-based accessor contracts) be stated for a bare `T: Address`: the
19. // address-family `View` impls are all `cfg(verus_keep_ghost)`-gated and the
20. // generic exec `impl<T: Address> ...` blocks carry no `View` bound, so a
21. // conditional `View<V = int>` bound would make `self@` untypable inside the
22. // accessors. `spec_page_size()` is the canonical page size, re-exported from
23. // `crate::hal::mem`.
24. 
25. verus! {
26. 
27. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
28. use crate::hal::mem::spec_addr;
29. 
30. // Abstract value of a memory region: the geometry `(start, size)` (in bytes,
31. // as mathematical integers) plus the three metadata tags callers observe.
32. pub struct MemoryRegionView {
33.     /// First valid byte address of the region. Equals the `start` supplied at
34.     /// construction; for the truncated variant it is page-aligned. Also the
35.     /// `Ord` key for both region types.
36.     pub start: int,
37.     /// Length of the region in bytes. The interval is `[start, start + size)`.
38.     /// For the truncated variant it is a multiple of the page size.
39.     pub size: int,
40.     /// Classification of the region (Usable / Reserved / Mmio / Bad).
41.     pub typ: MemoryRegionType,
42.     /// Access permissions granted over the region.
43.     pub perm: AccessPermission,
44.     /// Optional MMIO caching policy; `None` for non-MMIO regions.
45.     pub cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy>,
46. }
47. 
48. impl MemoryRegionView {
49.     /// Non-empty, non-wrapping interval lying within the address space. This is
50.     /// the geometry every constructed region guarantees and that caller
51.     /// arithmetic (`size - 1`, `start + size - 1`, `size / FRAME_SIZE`) relies
52.     /// on: `size >= 1` (`new` rejects `size == 0`) and the inclusive end
53.     /// `start + size - 1` never overflows the widest address representation.
54.     pub open spec fn wf_geometry(self) -> bool {
55.         &&& self.size >= 1
56.         &&& self.start >= 0
57.         &&& self.start + self.size <= usize::MAX as int + 1
58.     }
59. 
60.     /// Exclusive end of the half-open interval `[start, end)`.
61.     pub open spec fn spec_end(self) -> int {
62.         self.start + self.size
63.     }
64. 
65.     /// Inclusive last byte address (callers compute `start + size - 1`).
66.     pub open spec fn spec_last(self) -> int {
67.         self.start + self.size - 1
68.     }
69. 
70.     /// Whether `addr` lies in `[start, start + size)`.
71.     pub open spec fn contains(self, addr: int) -> bool {
72.         self.start <= addr < self.start + self.size
73.     }
74. 
75.     /// State transition of `MemoryRegion::set_cache_policy`: only the cache
76.     /// policy changes; geometry and the other tags are preserved (`..self`).
77.     pub open spec fn spec_set_cache_policy(self, policy: MmioCachePolicy) -> MemoryRegionView {
78.         MemoryRegionView { cache_policy: Some(policy), ..self }
79.     }
80. }
81. 
82. // `MemoryRegion<T>` abstracts to its geometry plus tags. The `view()` is
83. // `closed`: callers reference `self@.start` / `self@.size` but the field-to-
84. // storage mapping (and the `spec_addr` projection of the typed `start`) does not
85. // leak. Unconditional over `T: Address` (see module comment).
86. impl<T: Address> View for MemoryRegion<T> {
87.     type V = MemoryRegionView;
88. 
89.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> MemoryRegionView {
90.         MemoryRegionView {
91.             start: spec_addr(&self.start),
92.             size: self.size as int,
93.             typ: self.typ,
94.             perm: self.perm,
95.             cache_policy: self.cache_policy,
96.         }
97.     }
98. }
99. 
100. // `TruncatedMemoryRegion<T>` is the same interval with a stronger invariant; its
101. // `view()` forwards to the inner `MemoryRegion<PageAligned<T>>`.
102. impl<T: Address> View for TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
103.     type V = MemoryRegionView;
104. 
105.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> MemoryRegionView {
106.         self.0@
107.     }
108. }
109. 
110. // Well-formedness of a base memory region: non-empty, non-wrapping geometry.
111. impl<T: Address> MemoryRegion<T> {
112.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
113.         self@.wf_geometry()
114.     }
115. }
116. 
117. // Well-formedness of a truncated region: base geometry plus page alignment of
118. // both endpoints (established by `TruncatedMemoryRegion::new`'s `align_up`), so
119. // `size / FRAME_SIZE` is exact and `start` needs no re-alignment.
120. impl<T: Address> TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
121.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
122.         &&& self@.wf_geometry()
123.         &&& self@.start % spec_page_size() == 0

 `<T as Clone>::clone` — does **not compile** under Verus (it is structurally
 rejected; see the failed attempts below). Their cited precedent
 `<PageAligned<T> as Address>::into_raw_value` works only because its `Self` is a
 *concrete type constructor* (`PageAligned<T>`); for `clone` the receiver is a
 *bare type parameter* `T`, which Verus forbids.
 
 I therefore removed the `admit()` by eliminating the unprovable obligation at its
 root rather than trusting it. The accessor returns `self.start.clone()`; the
 obligation `spec_addr(&clone) == spec_addr(&self.start)` only existed because the
 value was *cloned* (and `Clone::clone` carries no value guarantee in vstd). Every
 `Address` implementor (`VirtualAddress`, `PhysicalAddress`, `PageAligned<T>`,
 `PageTableAligned<T>`) already derives `Copy`, so I:
 
 1. **`src/libs/sys/src/sys/mm/address/mod.rs:33`** — added `Copy` to the
    `Address` supertrait bound:
    ```rust
    Self: core::fmt::Debug + Clone + Copy + PartialEq + Eq + PartialOrd + Ord,
    ```
    This is satisfied by all four existing impls (the two generic ones derive
    `Copy` conditioned on `T: Copy`, which the new supertrait supplies). No `dyn
    Address` exists in the tree, so object-safety is unaffected.
 
 2. **`src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/region.rs:220-221`** — changed
    `MemoryRegion::start`'s body from `self.start.clone()` to a `Copy` field read
    `self.start`. With `T: Copy` a field read is **identity** in Verus
    (`result == self.start`), so `spec_addr(&result) == spec_addr(&self.start) ==
    self@.start` discharges by congruence — **no clone law, no `admit()`**. The
    `ensures` (`spec_addr(&result) == self@.start`) is unchanged and equally
    strong. `TruncatedMemoryRegion::start` delegates to this and inherits the
    guarantee.
 
 3. **`src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/region.spec.rs`** — removed the broken
    clone-spec experiments; the file holds only the View/inv/helpers.
 
 ### Verification

 baseline); the `sys` crate re-verified clean after the supertrait change.
 
 `./z build -- all` → **`[OK] Build complete.`** (dual compilation intact; the
 `Copy` read is valid in the normal build because `Address: Copy` now holds).
 
 ### Result: FIXED
 
 The `admit()` is gone, the `ensures` is byte-for-byte as strong, and both
 `make verify-kernel` and `make verify` exit 0 with `admit=0` for this module.

 #### Appendix — every approach tried for the reviewer's literal mechanism (all rejected by Verus)
 
 1. `pub assume_specification<T: Address>[ <T as Clone>::clone ](addr: &T) -> (result: T) ensures spec_addr(&result) == spec_addr(addr);`
    ```
    error: assume_specification cannot be used to specify generic specifications of trait methods; consider using external_trait_specification instead
    ```
 
 2. `external_trait_specification` proxy `ExAddressClone: Sized { type ExternalTraitSpecificationFor: Address; fn clone(&self) -> (result: Self) ensures spec_addr(&result) == spec_addr(self); }`
    ```
    error[E0277]: the trait bound `Self: sys::mm::Address` is not satisfied
    note: required by a bound in `...::spec_addr`
    ```
    (No proxy mechanism grants `Self: Address`, which `spec_addr<T: Address>` requires.)
 
 3. Same proxy but `ExAddressClone: Address`:
    ```
    error: external_trait_specification trait bound mismatch
    help: external_trait_specification requires trait bounds to match exactly ...
    ```

    ```

    ```
    (vstd already owns `Clone`'s spec via `ExClone`, with no value guarantee, and
    it cannot be overridden or strengthened for the `Address` subfamily.)
 
 These confirm a value-preservation guarantee cannot be attached to
 `Clone::clone` for a generic `T: Address`. Avoiding the clone entirely (the
 `Copy` field read) is the sound resolution and is what the final fix uses.
